ledgerSearch.outcome: CTD-0030 is decisive. The corpus alternately calls the first Cardinal Scale an imagined composite and an existing community of eighty-seven people three years into operation, and the item requires one accurate status used consistently with every existence-proof claim removed. The restoration therefore keeps the shipped design fiction statement verbatim and converts the baseline's Somewhere in the temperate uplands there is a watershed into an imagined watershed. CTD-0036 requires the direct-trust range and the bioregional population to stay distinct, which bears on the eighty-seven figure and is handled in Chapter Twenty-Seven. CTD-0029 concerns a promised separate account of the Cardinal Scale and was read; it governs Volume IX.

findings.summary: The image the section exists to plant was replaced by a specification of the scenario.

evidence.baseline: One image to carry from the start, because it is easier to build toward something you can see. ... It is not a utopia. It has hard winters and harder disagreements, software that does not always work, and people who arrive skeptical and stay that way for a while. What it has that the world outside it has largely lost is a way of keeping faith: with one another, with the land that holds them, with the generations not yet arrived.
evidence.shipped: The Cardinal Scale in this volume is a composite scenario. It places eighty-seven imagined participants in a temperate upland watershed and asks what the architecture would require of them. The scenario includes hard winters, stubborn disagreements, imperfect software, and decisions that leave no one fully satisfied.

findings.diagnosis: CTD-0030 requires that no existence-proof claim survive that the evidence does not support. It does not require the image to be replaced by an inventory. The baseline's list of hardships ends on the thing the community has that the world has lost, which is the sentence the whole image is for, and the shipped list ends on decisions that leave no one satisfied. Keeping faith with the generations not yet arrived is also the volume's dedication, returning here for the first time.

It is what we are building toward. Everything that follows is how.

The original record already judged it better stated than anything the baseline offers while filing it as a kept; under the ratified rule that judgment is a finding in the prior pass's favor, and this entry records it as one.

reasoning.note: R-LEDGER-WINS. CTD-0030 changes the grammar of the restoration rather than its content. There is a watershed becomes Imagine a watershed, and the shipped design fiction paragraph is kept as the section's closing statement so that the image and its status are never separated.

R-PUNCT-STRUCT. Four em dashes. Two introduced specifications and became colons, at keeping faith and at what the argument looks like. One was parenthetical and became a comma pair. One before the closing pair became a period.

The shipped statement that the scenes do not establish that a Cardinal Scale exists, that the named mechanisms have worked, or that the proposed outcomes have occurred. It is the ledger's requirement and it is better stated than anything the baseline offers.
The reason for planting the image, the not a utopia list with its landing on keeping faith, the four part promise of the returning thread, and the closing pair.

openQuestions:
STRUCTURAL RESTORATION BLOCKED ON ROUTE ADJUDICATION, not an editorial judgment. The introduction to PART ONE, the running prose between the part label The Sequence Problem and the first chapter heading beneath it, compiles into a chapter-start section with its own public route. Restoring the baseline's fuller introduction revives a section whose route was retired, and the same hazard applies here even though this part did not break. The introduction has therefore been reverted to its pre-edit state byte for byte and no part introduction anywhere in this volume was touched. Reassigning a canonical route and a reviewed successor is an author-facing continuity decision and this pass has no standing to make it.

WHAT STANDS NOW:

Part I concerns sequence. Projects often build governance before trust, technology before culture, or scale before proof. The order matters because sovereignty cannot be retrofitted into a data system, and constitutional limits are weakest when added after power has already formed.

The chapters that follow separate four problems: translating principle into buildable questions, testing one real community, growing without hollowing the design, and protecting long timeframes from immediate pressure.

WHAT THE BASELINE HAS, punctuation already repaired so it can be pasted in one edit once the route decision is made:

Volume III's opening diagnosed the failure of fragmented goodness: the structural condition in which enormous amounts of regenerative intelligence remain unable to coordinate at the scales required, not because the intelligence does not exist but because the infrastructure for coordinating it has not been built. That diagnosis was the necessary first work. It established that the coordination crisis is structural rather than moral, and that the response must therefore be architectural rather than exhortatory.

Volume IV begins at the next failure, the one that follows diagnosis, follows design, follows the completion of the map. It is the failure of wrong sequence. Projects that build governance before trust has formed. Projects that build technology before the culture that will inhabit the technology exists. Projects that attempt planetary scale before local proof of concept has demonstrated that the architecture actually works when real people with real stakes live inside it. This failure is so consistent across the history of transformational infrastructure that it must be understood not as a collection of individual mistakes but as a structural pattern requiring its own architectural response.

The sequence is not negotiable. It follows from the architecture itself. Trust cannot be added to a system later as a feature. Constitutional coherence cannot be imposed on a project that grew without it and then rationalized afterward. Sovereignty cannot be retrofitted into a data architecture that was not built for it from the beginning. These are not operational preferences. They are structural facts about how the layers of the architecture relate to one another.

The four chapters of Part I examine what must come first and why; what a genuine first embodiment of the architecture requires; how the scaling transition can be navigated without destroying what made the early community worth scaling; and how an institution operating across radically different timeframes, daily, decadal, generational, civilizational, maintains coherence across all of them simultaneously. Each chapter takes up where Volume III left the question and moves it from the level of design principle to the level of construction requirement.

WHAT THE CURRENT TEXT LOSES: the diagnosis of fragmented goodness this part builds on, the four named sequence failures, the argument that trust cannot be added later and sovereignty cannot be retrofitted, and the four chapter map.

TO RESTORE: the prose change and the continuity change must land together. The section id minted by the restored introduction needs a canonical route and a reviewed successor recorded in publishing/continuity/section-lineage.json in the same edit.

The restored line It is what we are building toward is a first person plural commitment about a community the same section says is imagined. The two are compatible, since one can build toward a design, but the sentence sits one word away from an existence claim and the author should decide whether CTD-0030 wants it bounded further.

The baseline heading, The Cardinal Scale, Seen From Here, carries the image. The shipped heading, The Cardinal Scale as Design Fiction, carries the ledger. Both are defensible and the route belongs to the second.

The volume-04 voice card was prepared by the same pass that produced the shipped text, and its exemplar anchors and protected lines quote that text rather than the baseline. The card records `Author approved: pending tone, strategy, heading, and overcompression review`. The restoration keeps every line the card protects and otherwise follows the baseline, which means card and source now diverge in wording the card does not name. R-VOICE-BIND requires that the disagreement be raised rather than settled here: the card should be re-derived from whichever text the author approves.

Structural labels were frozen for this pass and none was touched. Every markdown heading, every standalone bold display line, every chapter label, and every all-capital display line is byte identical to its pre-edit state, in the same order, with the same blank-line separators on both sides. A label determines a section id, a section id is a public route, and `publishing/continuity/section-lineage.json` already records this volume's renames and resolves the historical routes. Changing one is a continuity decision and not an editorial one. Only the running prose between labels was restored. Where a baseline label names its section better than the current one, the cost is recorded here and the label is left alone.

regenerationTest.purpose: The rules must reproduce the section from the baseline without consulting the shipped text.
regenerationTest.method: Derived from the immutable baseline applying editorial/method/standard.md, the corpus voice card, the volume-04 voice card, and the debt ledger under R-LEDGER-WINS.
regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required. The section is the volume's model case for a high severity item that constrains modality without constraining content: CTD-0030 governs whether the community is said to exist, not whether it may be described. Separating those two questions is what allowed the image to come back intact while the paydown held.

audits.auditor: editorial-agent, generation 1 of the twenty-rule re-render lane
audits.scope: Full re-read of the current section against the immutable baseline under all twenty rules. The original record was derived under the thirteen-rule index; this audit adds the substitution count and the later rules: R-LEDGER-WINS-COROLLARY, R-CORRECTION-SCOPE, R-CANON-DELETION-RECORD, R-PAIRED-DELETION, R-CAUTIOUS-HALF, R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT, and R-REFRAIN-COST.

substitutionTest.rule: R-CAUTIOUS-HALF, substitution form, run as standing procedure before any pairing test
substitutionTest.method: Normalize both texts, strip markup, split into sentences of three or more words, count baseline sentences appearing verbatim in the current section.
substitutionTest.note: Well above zero, so the section is a restoration, not a substitution, and the pairing test applies. Verbatim survival understates fidelity here: every R-PUNCT-STRUCT repair and recorded bounding changes the sentence it lands in, so the non-surviving remainder was read against the diff and attributed rather than assumed lost.

audits.checked: R-CORRECTION-SCOPE: CTD-0030's grammar conversion was verified at width: There is a watershed became Imagine a watershed, live existence verbs stayed inside the imagined frame, and the surrounding image prose is otherwise the baseline's. One knock-on divergence is attributed below. R-CANON-DELETION-RECORD: the unrestored part introduction is quoted in full in the original record's open question with its route cost, which satisfies the rule for the one deliberate non-restoration here; the structural hold on part introductions is absolute in this volume and this audit re-verified the introduction is byte identical to its pre-edit state. R-CAUTIOUS-HALF: the section keeps both the image half and the caution half, It is not a utopia beside the keeping-faith landing, and the closing pair keeps its commitment, It is what we are building toward. R-PAIRED-DELETION: Cardinal Scale, watershed, eighty-seven, and keeping faith were swept; every referent the returning-thread promise names, funding, governance, capture, success, has a restored chapter. R-REFRAIN-COST: the returning thread is the coda run's successor and is recorded once at v04-coda-in-plain-terms; this record's promise sentence now points at scenario chapters that exist. R-TENSE: eighty-seven people are learning is a live condition inside an explicit imagining, correct as it stands. R-DEIXIS, R-NEGATION-STACK, R-LEDGER-WINS-COROLLARY: nothing fires.
audits.conclusion: The restoration holds under the full twenty-rule index. Eight of thirty baseline sentences survive verbatim, the lowest count in the volume's prose sections, and the gap is fully attributed: the CTD-0030 grammar conversion, the unrestored part introduction held under the structural rule, the retired coda placement, and the recorded punctuation repairs. One substitution credit recorded as F3. No prose change required.
corrections: One divergence the original record did not itemize: the baseline's promise to return to the Cardinal Scale at the close of nearly every chapter stands as through the book. The baseline placement was the coda system's, which CTD-0095 retired, so the reworded promise is the only version the current volume can keep. Attributed here rather than silent.
